pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Irregular, multi-pointed polygonal shapes with high angularity and star-like projections. Edges exhibit sharp pixel gradients transitioning from dark brown to light cream. Patch size varies from large, complex shapes on the mid-flank to smaller, more condensed units toward the ventral and limb regions.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of light tan pathways forming a topological web. Intersection nodes are frequent, predominantly 3-way junctions. Pixel thickness of the corridors is relatively uniform across the mid-flank, maintaining clear separation between dark patches.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: Low-amplitude, high-frequency bristled fringe along the neck and shoulder. The silhouette shows a dense, short-cropped texture against the background.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: A localized discontinuity in the mane profile is visible at the base of the neck, coinciding with the position of a perched avian subject.

other_distinctive_markers: Presence of at least four avian subjects (oxpeckers) clinging to the dorsal ridge and upper flank, creating localized points of anatomical occlusion.
